Subject: Urgent: Production latency & error spike - checkout flows

Team,

Starting ~07:45 PT we're seeing a sudden and sustained increase in 95/99p latency across the checkout API calls that hit Redwood for payment tokenization. Error rate for those requests jumped from ~0.3% to 4.2% and throughput dropped (timeouts) for about 30% of requests routed to us. This is affecting 3 regional backends for us (us-west/us-central/us-east).

Impact: 
- Checkout timeouts -> increased cart abandonment across web/mobile (observed in last 35m).
- Multiple customers reporting failed authorizations (we've paged billing ops).

We captured traces and a short pcap; attaching a snippet below. Can you confirm if this is a Redwood runtime/regression or if any recent model rollouts could be contributing?

Attachments: telemetry_snippet.txt (included in link below)

Please advise immediate next steps and ETA. This is a Sev-1 for Hypertide.

— Alex
Alex Rivera

On Sat, Dec 5, 2026 at 08:12 AM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@hypertide.com> wrote:
> Starting ~07:45 PT we're seeing a sudden and sustained increase in 95/99p latency...

Initial findings (08:29):
- No model rollout recorded at 07:30–07:50 PT across the managed model registry for Hypertide's pinned model. Verified via deployment audit log.
- Runtime telemetry: a spike in KV cache misses for the tokenization route beginning 07:44; sustained concurrent request fan-in caused GPU-side scheduling backpressure.
- We see a surge of ~2.7x for long-context requests (client-side); sequence-length distribution shifted from median 64 -> median 420 across the affected calls. This explains abnormal token generation time and elevated memory churn.
- Autoscaler events: multiple short-lived allocation failures in us-west (OOM attempts) — likely because longer contexts pinned more KV state.

Attachments: telemetry_report_20261205.pdf (contains heatmaps, p99 traces)

Immediate mitigations applied (08:27–08:32):
- Temporarily throttled max input sequence length for Hypertide route to 256 (config override) — reduces KV pressure.
- Lifted burst capacity in Dedicated pool for Hypertide (requested +2 GPU nodes from pool).
- Enabled aggressive KV prefix caching to favor repeated token streams.

Next steps (in parallel):
1) Capture and share a compact trace bundle for Hypertide for 07:40–08:10 PT.
2) Work with Marissa on customer-friendly explanation and ETA for full fix.
3) Engineering to prepare a permanent guardrail: implement a sequence-length based routing policy to avoid scheduling pressure.

I'll upload the telemetry bundle to the shared drive and update JIRA SUP-4821.

— Karthik
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

Team — thank you for the quick triage. Summary for exec stakeholders and Hypertide: 

What happened (so far): 
- Root cause appears to be an unexpected skew to very long client payloads driving KV cache miss pressure and short-lived OOMs in a subset of Dedicated nodes (us-west primarily). No model code regression detected.

Actions taken: 
- Temporary config guard applied (max sequence cap 256) to reduce memory churn.
- +2 Dedicated GPUs provisioned as immediate headroom in us-west; autoscaler tuning in progress.
- Engineering developing a long-term routing rule to route long-context sessions to a higher-memory variant and prevent fan-in.

Customer comms plan: 
- Marissa: share a concise status note with Hypertide now (15–20m cadence), then a 1-hour follow-up that includes a remediation ETA.
- Lauren (exec): I'll inform Sales leadership and the customer executive sponsor that we have an active strike team and are treating this as Sev-1. If Hypertide wants a daily post-mortem, we'll offer a joint exec readout.

Please ensure JIRA SUP-4821 is updated with timestamps and the telemetry bundle. Marissa, copy me on the next customer-facing message.

— Lauren
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya — thank you for flagging this. Short status update for Hypertide: 

Where we are (11:03 PT):
- Incident: Elevated p95/p99 latency and error rate on checkout tokenization route observed between 07:44–08:40 PT.
- What we did: Applied a temporary sequence-length cap (256) to reduce memory pressure and enabled aggressive KV caching; provisioned +2 Dedicated GPUs in us-west to absorb backlog.
- Customer impact: Client-facing timeouts have dropped to baseline for ~85% of traffic; a small residual percentage of requests still experience elevated latency while backlog drains.

What to expect next: 
- We will keep the transient caps in place for up to 4 hours while we complete a safe routing change that funnels long-context sessions to a larger-memory variant. Planned completion: ~15:00 PT today.
- Karthik will deliver the full telemetry bundle and a short technical postmortem in JIRA SUP-4821 by EOD.

Attachments: telemetry_report_20261205.pdf, span_logs_segment_61.zip

If you want an immediate bridge (voice), we can join Hypertide SREs now — otherwise we'll continue with 15m email cadence and send the 1h status update at ~12:05 PT.
